Before Seattle’s music scene became history, lancemphoto was there to document it. Join OfficialAment and AmesBros at easystreetrecords tomorrow for a conversation moderated by Lance, revisiting those formative years and Pearl Jam’s rise revealed through never-before-seen photos in the new memoir, Since Forever.

items.title_orig: I lose respect for anyone who thinks TTPD was a good album
items.article_text:
First off, I know that some songs are poetic ("Hallelujah" comes to mind) but I would prefer if we stop calling songs poems. We don't call poems songs, so let's just stop. Robert Frost wasn't a songwriter, he was a poet. Taylor isn't a poet, she is a songwriter. Songwriters shouldn't win literary awards unless they write poetry or novels and poets shouldn't win music awards unless they write song lyrics. It matters what things are.
 Second, the album was, not long ago, sitting at a 66 on Metacritic (too high in my opinion) and was critically panned. It's now a 75 on Metacritic and I feel like the world is trying to gaslight me. Did a bunch of Swifties become critics? Is everyone trying to make me think TTPD was competent when I recall everyone mocking how absurd and bloated the album was?
